To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the CAP1 and CAP2 prototypes are the first monolithic active pixel devices designed to operate in a high radiation environment and to have the readout speed to match a B-factory vertex detector, (ii) the CAP1 prototype has a hit efficiency of 98.8% and the CAP2 prototype has a hit occupancy of 1.2% with an efficiency of 99.9%, (iii) the CAP2 prototype shows a 1.5% threshold shift
we have designed and fabricated two monolithic active-pixellated devices in the 0.35/spl mu/m CMOS TSMC process.

(1) a 0.35/spl mu/m MAPS process has been developed with radiation hardness comparable to that of the 1/spl mu/m process and (2) a prototype pixel sensor with a deep sampling pipeline and correlated double sampling readout has been developed that is capable of operating in the presence of a high occupancy rate and high leakage current
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of monolithic pixel devices.
the development of an integrated pixel sensor for the KEK B-factory upgrade.
the development and evaluation of a MAPS-based vertex detector for a future B-factory upgrade.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MAPS are indeed a viable technology for the next generation of vertex detectors at a B-factory.
these devices are a very promising technology for future vertex detectors at the upgraded KEK-B facility.
the MAPS technology is ready to be implemented in a vertex detector for a high-luminosity B-factory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully demonstrated a monolithic pixel detector with radiation hardness, high speed readout, and low occupancy.
the CAP2 architecture, with its deep sampling pipeline, is an excellent candidate for the vertex detector upgrade at KEK-B.
the CAP architecture has proven to be a very promising technology for the Belle vertex detector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAP2 design, with 8-bit depth, is the most promising for future vertex detectors at the KEK-B factory.
the TSMC process appears to have the radiation hardness needed for a MAPS-based vertex detector.
a MAPS device with a sampling pipeline is a promising candidate for a vertex detector in a high luminosity environment.
